records.name: Singapore
records.summary_text:
Singapore is broadly workable — far safer than its neighbour Malaysia, with no criminalisation of trans identity, no religious police, and one of the world's lowest crime rates. Section 377A (which criminalised sex between men) was repealed in 2022, and the prison service reports no assaults against its 10 transgender inmates — unusually positive for axis-H. Singapore is also a regional medical hub with gender-affirming care available.

records.name: Iran
records.summary_text: Iran is one of the world's most severe environments for trans people — but with a unique bifurcation. Same-sex conduct carries the death penalty, and a trans woman was raped in Ministry of Intelligence custody (the documented case of Ghazal Marzban in Evin Prison, 2023). The Tehran City Council ordered trans people to avoid "busy" areas of the capital. Trans people who have not had surgery face immorality and indecency provisions (imprisonment, fines, lashes) and documented forced-transition pressure — 6Rang describes "40 years of forcing gay people to choose between transitioning and death
